severity_definitions.P0: Sai claim học thuật, attribution/CLO, điểm/achievement hoặc nâng scope/learning verb; reference bịa/sai nguồn.
severity_definitions.P1: Thiếu bằng chứng hoặc correction cho claim đúng, thiếu phân biệt/coverage/completeness/scope.
severity_definitions.P2: Vấn đề trình bày, lặp hoặc naturalness, không đổi kết luận học thuật.

findings.description: Explicitly says ADY201m/CLO7 mentions API in its workflow; the canonical CLO7 does not name API. Historical attribution error is repeated.
DAP391m/CLO7 remains under API evidence without clarifying its data-project role; quoted ADY201m/CLO3 at-least-one statement has no CLO3 reference.
Tool limits are explained correctly, but does not explicitly discuss the named PFP191/DBI202 tool contexts requested in the probe.
Long full-English CLO quotations and a repetitive opening/conclusion reduce conversational naturalness.
ADY201m/CLO7 and DAP391m/CLO7 are still grouped under API evidence; wording only gives project context, not a false direct API claim, but does not explicitly correct the old attribution.
Explains ADY201m/CLO3 use-at-least-one rule without citing CLO3; DAP391m/CLO6 wording 'cho thấy năng lực' is stronger than the bounded learning-outcome wording requested.
Repeats tools/professional-use limitations in separate sections and conclusion; lengthy quotations.
Clarifies API is in ADY201m/CLO5 and project context in CLO7, but keeps DAP391m/CLO7 under API without clearly separating it from DAP391m/CLO6's Watson API outcome.
Offers an evidence map for CV review at the end, outside the requested V1 academic/JD scope; no CV is actually produced.
Explanations repeat across six sections and include an unnecessary follow-up offer.

CPV paragraph says outcomes confirm 'học và triển khai ... segmentation, object detection, tracking'. CPV301/CLO5 is Understand segmentation; CLO9 is Explain face recognition/tracking. The grouped wording upgrades those learning verbs and cites only CPV metadata.tools for that paragraph, not the outcome descriptions.
PFP191 fundamentals/data structures/file handling/OOP claims have only PFP191 metadata.tools reference, not the relevant PFP191 CLOs.
Repeats tools/alternatives/professional limits across several long sections and ends with an unnecessary follow-up offer; detail is not itself penalized.
